description: Trend Matrix AI is a solo team building an interactive Earth science dashboard for the 'Be an Earth System Trend Detective!' challenge. Powered by a Python/Flask backend, SQLite database, and Chart.js frontend, our platform visualizes climate datasets like global temperatures and rainfall. We integrate Gemini API as an intelligent Trend Explainer to convert statistical metrics into simple, accessible insights for students and the general public.
summary:
TrendMatrix AI is an interactive Earth Systems Trend Intelligence Platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It helps users explore historical environmental observations, investigate long-term trends, and better understand changes in Earth's systems.

Using NASA POWER data, the platform currently analyzes five environmental variables: air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, precipitation, and solar radiation. Users can select geographic coordinates through an interactive 3D Earth globe or search for a location, choose a date range, and explore daily or monthly observations.

TrendMatrix AI applies statistical methods, including linear regression, Mann-Kendall testing, Sen's slope estimation, and Newey-West standard errors, to investigate trend direction, magnitude, and statistical significance. Interactive visualizations and automatically generated scientific reports make the results easier to understand.

The platform is designed for students, educators, researchers, and the public, making Earth observation data more accessible for environmental exploration and evidence-based understanding of change.
details:
Project Details

What the Project Does

TrendMatrix AI is an interactive web-based platform that helps users investigate long-term changes in Earth's environmental systems using historical Earth observation data. Users can select a location through an interactive 3D Earth globe or search for a place, choose a date range, and analyze environmental observations.

How It Works

The platform retrieves daily environmental observations from the NASA POWER API for selected geographic coordinates. Its current live analysis supports five variables: air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, precipitation, and solar radiation.

Users can explore daily or monthly data through interactive visualizations. Statistical techniques, including linear regression, the Mann-Kendall test, Sen's slope estimation, and Newey-West standard errors, help investigate trend direction, magnitude, and statistical significance. The platform also generates scientific HTML reports containing analysis results and supporting information.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Trend Matrix AI makes environmental data easier to explore and understand. It can support:

  • Students and educators: Learning about climate and environmental trends through real observations.
  • Researchers: Exploring historical environmental patterns and conducting preliminary trend investigations.
  • Environmental analysts: Examining changes in selected environmental variables over time.
  • The public: Building awareness of changes in Earth's systems through accessible visualizations.

Technology and Tools

The project uses Python, Flask, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Statsmodels, pymannkendall, SQLite, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Plotly. Globe.gl provides the interactive 3D Earth interface. NASA POWER provides the live environmental observations, while Photon supports location search. Google Gemini API is included as an optional AI explanation component.

Creativity and Innovation

The platform brings geographic location selection, NASA environmental observations, statistical trend investigation, interactive charts, and automated scientific reporting together in one interface. It aims to make scientific exploration more approachable without hiding the statistical methods behind the results.

Current Limitations

The live analysis currently supports five NASA POWER variables and retrieves point-based observations for selected coordinates, not regional averages. NDVI, evapotranspiration, and soil moisture have been explored separately using NASA AppEEARS data but are not yet integrated into the live analysis pipeline. The 3D globe is a geographic selector, not a satellite imagery or raster-data map. The optional Gemini explanation feature depends on an external service and may not always be available.

Future Improvements

Future development may include integrating additional NASA Earth observation variables, comparing multiple locations, adding satellite data layers and spatial analysis, improving seasonal analysis, and strengthening AI-generated scientific explanations.
